profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer (EA Directorate) at Amentum (Formerly Jacobs Technology)
profile.summary:
Professional Technical Skills Summary:
Highly accomplished Senior Embedded Software Engineer with 40+ years of experience designing, integrating, and verifying avionics and spaceflight software. Mid-Level Software Engineer in real-time operating systems (RTOS), hardware/software co-design, and military/aerospace communication protocols (MIL-STD-1553B, TTEthernet). Proven track record of delivering flight-ready embedded systems for high-consequence NASA Johnson Space Center platforms and environments. Possess advanced analysis and problem solving skills in software development (design, implementation, and test), systems integration, and system engineering. Possess a resourceful, creative, and result-oriented approach to conceiving, developing, and implementing resolution of issues in mature complex software and software/hardware systems. Possess journeyman experience of electronics design, hardware interfaces, hardware devices, and trouble-shooting at the board-level and component level repair using schematic analysis and oscilloscopes.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer (EA Directorate)
positions.description:
•
TTE Cyclic Phase Lock (CPL): Developed a hybrid TTE CPL by merging TTE CPL and Spacecraft Software Engineering Branch (FSW) implementations.
•
RTOS Performance Optimization: Developed VxWorks tasks to profile and optimize Best Effort (BE) shared memory utilization; validated network configuration parameters under a strict 25ms read/write constraint.
•
Network Protocol Verification: Architected VxWorks tasks to analyze concurrent multi-transmitter data flows into single sampling ports, successfully verifying 40Hz minor frame data overwrites to guarantee zero-latency data processing.
•
Hardware/Firmware Integration – EMU Data Recorder
o
Developed embedded C&DH firmware for an Extravehicular Mobility Unit (spacesuit) Data Recorder utilizing an MSP430 microcontroller.
o
Engineered a data pipeline to collect, packetize, and store 7Hz diagnostic data streaming from an optical UART interface onto a microSD card.
o
Implemented low-power wireless telemetry using a Redpine Signals 802.11 b/g SoC to transmit data to the ISS network upon command.
•
Secure Communications: Built an IPC component for an active ionizing radiation monitor running on a Xilinx Virtex-IV PowerPC platform, leveraging MIL-STD-1553B primary interfaces and redundant UNIX/TCP-IP socket.
•
Avionics Modernization: Enhanced and rehosted legacy SAFER Avionics Software for the ISS 24-jet free-flyer self-contained EVA propulsion system, ensuring critical maneuvering capabilities for crew members.

positions.title: Systems Software Engineer
positions.description:
Contracts include: United Space Alliance (USA), 1099 Consulting, Loral, STSOC, Unisys, Lockheed, Computer Sciences Corp (CSC)
•
RTLS Abort Software: Programmed ground-based near-real-time Shuttle Return to Launch Site (RTLS) trajectory logic using IBM 360/370 Basic Assembly Language.
•
Network Infrastructure: Programmed TCP/IP and UDP implementations on DEC VAX/VMS minicomputers to modernize the Johnson Space Center Engineering and Science Network (JESNET) pipeline.
•
Telemetry Formatting: Sustained and enhanced embedded C code on Intel 8086 processors for Micro Instrumentation and Telemetry Systems (MITS) Lan custom IBM Series/1 telemetry cards. These cards captured raw, high-speed synchronous serial data streams straight from the Shuttle tracking networks (such as TDRSS or ground stations) and packetized the data into standard formats.
•
Debris Tracking: Debris Tracking: Co-developed and architected the "COMM Manager" pipeline to ingest and process high-throughput space situational awareness (SSA) data for Air Force debris tracking. Development was in “C” on a Motorola 68030-based Masscomp system running real-time UNIX (RTU) heavily modified by MASSCOMP/Concurrent for deterministic, low-latency, real-time multiprocessing.
•
Shuttle/ISS Sustaining: Sustained and enhanced the Information Sharing Protocol (ISP) for Ground Based Systems for Plug-in Port Utilization Officer (PLUTO) Discipline. ISP is the distributed computing foundation for the mission control center.

projects.title: MISL
projects.description: The Modular Integrated Stackable Layers (MISL) is a compact space-rated computer system that is modular, scalable and reconfigurable. The original goal was to design a space environment capable instrumentation system with a flexible design so that as subsets of requirements changed, it minimized the need for new designs and maximized the reusability of the hardware and software modules. The result is a flexible, economical and small computer system that can be adapted to uses in space environment instrumentation and control.
